newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude, product futures bounce back a bit.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude, product futures bounce back a bit.

text.p: NYMEX crude and oil product futures ended firmer Thursday, helped by an outage at Tosco Corp's Bayway, New Jersey plant, though market players see further losses next week as likely.
In fairly thin trding, January crude futures settled at $23.72, up 33 cents on the day and pulling back a bit of the $2.50 losses seen over the last few days.

Thursday's price action held within Wednesday's wide $24.47/$23.15 range and more profit-taking gains are expected on Friday, though market participants generally see a weaker market next week if present trends continue.

"Look for support at $23.10 and $22.75 ahead of the $22.25 low from November 6," said Tim Evans, an analyst at Pegasus Econometrics in New York. However, he adds, "book-squaring ahead of the weekend is likely to feature buying tomorrow (Friday) as well."

The gains on Thursday were supported after Tosco said that the fluid catalytic cracking (FCC) unit at its Bayway, New Jersey plant went down. An unspecified problem there caused a small fire and sources familiar with company operations couldn't say when it would be back up.
The FCC there is among the largest and most sophisticated in the world, with a rated capacity of 140,000 barrels per day (bpd) out of a total plant processing capacity of 290,000 bpd.

It was unclear what the market impact would be, however, as December looks like being an exceptionally heavy month for gasoline imports, traders said. The cash market differential firmed up early in the day as well as futures prices, but had been very weak even before the NYMEX contracts were hit this week.
"A lot of large speculators saw refiners a few days ago selling cracks. (They) are buying back products and selling crude to cover those" and take profits, said Gerry Samuels of ARB Oil.
